ISO/IEC 42001:2023 requires an organization to establish, implement, maintain, document and continually improve an AI management system (AIMS). It applies to organizations of any size or type that provide or use products or services involving AI. [IEC overview](https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/90574)

In practice, the AIMS covers:

- **Organizational context and leadership:** identify relevant internal and external issues, interested parties and their requirements; define the AIMS scope; and set an AI policy, roles and responsibilities.
- **Planning:** set AI objectives and address AI risks and opportunities.
- **Support and operation:** provide resources and competence, maintain relevant documented information, and put processes and controls in place for AI systems across their lifecycle.
- **Performance and improvement:** monitor and evaluate the AIMS, conduct internal audits and management reviews, address nonconformities, and continually improve.

The standard also includes Annex A controls and Annex B implementation guidance on areas such as AI impact assessment, data governance, lifecycle management, transparency, and third-party relationships. The organization determines which controls are appropriate to its context and risks. [ISO guide](https://www.iso.org/insights/iso-42001-explained)

In short, it requires a documented, organization-wide way to govern AI and manage its risks—not a single technical control or a guarantee that every AI system is risk-free.
